ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List (Russia, Belarus, Mali, and others), and domestic Terrorism Designation List; PEP status determination under AML/CFT Act 2009 s 22(1)(c) requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval for high-risk clients.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use the Latin alphabet; names may include English letters and digits; Māori and other transliterated languages are permitted; the name must be in romanized script and must not be misleading. Suffix restrictions apply: company name must end with 'Limited' or 'Tāpui' (Māori for Limited).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office refuses a name reservation, the applicant may request a written reason under s 22(7) Companies Act 1993; file a formal response or revised name application through the Companies Office portal; if rejection is maintained, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 or pursue appeal rights as set out in s 22A (if applicable). Prior ministerial approval is required for any prohibited or sensitive token and must be submitted with the relevant government agency consent letter.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only if a substantial physical registered office with physical records, not a P.O. registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual probability for a fully compliant ordinary trading company; increases to 20–30% for cross-border high-value mineral trading due to AML/CFT medium-risk enhanced classification and associated monitoring by the Department of Internal Affairs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105): s 12 (mode of incorporation), s 13 (incorporation by registration), s 15 (name and NZBN), s 16 (certificate of incorporation), s 36 (registered office), ss 38-44 (appointment and duties of directors), s 49 (no par value shares), s 52 (issue of shares), s 73 (consideration for issue of shares), s 180 (execution of documents), s 194 (accounting records), Sch 1 (default constitution); Financial Reporting Act 2013 ss 17-21; Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 51 (registration threshold).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Business Registries, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Level 6, 12-16 Nicholls Lane, Auckland 1010, New Zealand; online portal: iservice.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZCN046) filed electronically through the Companies Office online incorporation service; Certificate of Incorporation issued electronically by the Registrar of Companies under s 16 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under New Zealand law. The company may be incorporated with a nominal subscribed capital of one (1) ordinary share per subscriber at NZ$1.00 each, issued as fully paid at incorporation. Consideration for the issue of shares must be known and received before allotment under s 73 of the Companies Act 1993; capital may be contributed in cash or in kind, and no capital duty or escrow deposit applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: COMPANY: CK_IC International Company (New Zealand) Limited; MEETING: First Meeting of the Board of Directors; VENUE/DATE: [Address, New Zealand] / [Date], held by video conference. RESOLVED THAT: 1. CONSTITUTION: The constitution presented to the meeting is hereby adopted as the definitive constitution of the Company pursuant to s 28 of the Companies Act 1993, and the directors are authorised to lodge the same with the New Zealand Companies Office. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The subscribers named in the incorporation application be and are hereby allotted the number of fully paid ordinary shares set out opposite their respective names in the register of shareholders; the directors are authorised to issue share certificates and to record the allotment in the share register. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [registered office street address, New Zealand], and the Registrar is directed to file the notice of registered office address under s 36 of the Companies Act 1993. 4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: The following persons be and are hereby appointed to hold office until the next annual shareholders' meeting: [Name] as sole director, [Name] as Chair of the Board, [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary (if any), each holding office subject to the constitution and applicable law. 5. BANK ACCOUNTS: The directors be and are hereby authorised to open and operate corporate bank accounts with a New Zealand registered bank; any two (2) of the following authorised signatories, namely [Names], shall execute withdrawals, transfers, mandates and foreign-exchange transactions, with an electronic banking transaction limit of NZ$250,000 per authorised instruction. 6. EXECUTION OF DOCUMENTS: Pursuant to s 180 of the Companies Act 1993, the directors be and are hereby authorised to execute all contracts, bills of lading, letters of credit, purchase agreements, warehousing agreements and customs declarations relating to the cross-border procurement and arbitrage of battery-grade lithium carbonate, including the affixation of the common seal (if adopted) attested by the director and secretary. 7. RATIFICATION OF PROMOTERS' ACTS: All preliminary acts taken by the promoters, the registered agent and legal counsel, including name reservation, constitution drafting and engagement of the business-bank relationship, be and are hereby ratified and approved in all respects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Available-Name Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, NZBN Register (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search on the NZBN register to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Submit a name reservation online through the Companies Office portal (fee NZ$10 per 20-working-day reservation). Where the name contains restricted words (e.g., 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance'), obtain prior written consent from the relevant supervisory authority. Retain the reservation number for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to three alternatives)
Consent letters for restricted words, if applicable
Subscriber identity particulars (name, address, date of birth)
Name reservation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a name-objection notice, respond in writing through the Companies Office correspondence channel within 10 working days; alternatively, withdraw the objectionable name and file an amended reservation. An administrative review request preserves the original time-stamp priority until the review is determined.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Compliance Officer / Authorised Legal Counsel (filed with Companies Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution in compliance with Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993, covering share capital and class rights, director powers and indemnities, share transfer restrictions, financial reporting elections and amendment procedures. Each subscriber must execute the constitution, and each proposed director must execute a consent to act as director (Form NZCN045). Prepare the draft register of shareholders and register of directors, and obtain certified copies of subscriber passports and proof of address (apostilled for non-New Zealand residents).
required_dossiers: Final constitution executed by all subscribers
Director consent to act (Form NZCN045) for each director
Certified passport copies and proof of residential address
Draft register of shareholders and directors
AML/KYC information certificate for subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the registrar or counsel identifies an inconsistency with the Companies Act (e.g., unconstitutional indemnity), issue a revised constitution and file a rectification application under s 21 of the Companies Act 1993. No additional state filing fee is charged for a governance-document correction if the original application is still pending.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Application (Form NZCN046)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Online Incorporation Service (iservice.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZCN046). Enter the proposed name, registered office street address (physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box), principal place of business, director details (at least one director resident in New Zealand or Australia; alternatively appoint a New Zealand resident agent for service of process), shareholder details and allotment of shares. Attach the executed constitution and director consent forms. Pay the NZ$150 registration fee via credit card or POLi. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and automatically allocates the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Form NZCN046 (electronic submission)
Executed constitution attached
Form NZCN045 consent of each director
Registered office address confirmation (NZCN040), if separate from principal place
Payment authorisation for registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a Notice of Proposed Refusal, the applicant may make written submissions within 10 working days. If the application remains deficient, the fee is refunded and the filing is voided; a fresh application may be submitted with the corrected data and a new priority time-stamp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and confirm the NZBN. Register the Company with the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number using Form IR742 (non-resident company) or IR596 (resident company, as applicable). Apply for Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration in the myIR portal if annual NZ taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZ$60,000; if the company is a pure offshore procurement vehicle with no NZ supplies, apply for a GST exemption certificate under s 56 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation notice
Form IR742 or IR596 as applicable
Director identification documents
Registered office certificate and bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number or GST registration is delayed beyond the SLA, escalate via the IRD online 'Contact us' channel quoting the NZBN; registration may be backdated where the application is lodged within 20 working days of the triggering transaction. A formal complaint may be lodged with the Ombudsman where delay causes demonstrable prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises, Civil Defence and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); Local Territorial Authority Building Consent Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the shell/International Company with no industrial plant, no manufacturing licence is required. If a registered office or liaison office is leased in New Zealand, notify the local Territorial Authority, obtain the building's Warrant of Fitness (where the building exceeds 100m² or has a compliance schedule), file a fire evacuation scheme with FENZ (Form 12) where more than 10 persons workshare, and adopt a written Health and Safety at Work policy together with a hazard register under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Where goods are never landed in New Zealand, no Worksafe notification for a 'prescribed high-risk activity' is required.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or occupation deed
Building Warrant of Fitness / compliance schedule (if applicable)
FENZ fire evacuation scheme application (Form 12)
Health and Safety at Work policy and hazard register
Electrical safety certificate for any occupied premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where FENZ or the Territorial Authority issues an inspection deficiency or improvement notice, remedy the stated non-compliance within 14 days and submit a corrective compliance schedule certified by an Independent Qualified Person (IQP). A cancellation or suspension of the evacuation scheme may be appealed to FENZ within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: HSNO / Customs Compliance Notification for Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand (EPA); New Zealand Customs Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess the hazardous-substance status of battery-grade lithium carbonate (CAS 554-13-2) under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Act 1996. For pure cross-border procurement and arbitrage with no physical landing in New Zealand, no importation approval is triggered; the activity is classified as a trading-only exemption. If the company elects to store, re-package or trans-ship the material in New Zealand, submit a Hazardous Substance Notification to the EPA under ss 96-97 HSNO Act, and obtain a Customs Controlled Area Licence under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 for any bonded warehouse. Register with NZ Customs for an Importer/Exporter Client Code for all declarations.
required_dossiers: Chemical Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for lithium carbonate
EPA Hazardous Substance Notification application (if warehousing in NZ)
NZ Customs Client Code registration form
Certificate of Analysis (battery grade, purity not less than 99.5%)
Incoterms contract and transport conformity certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EPA requests further information under s 68 HSNO Act, respond with a supplementary exposure-risk assessment within 30 working days; a deemed refusal or conditional approval may be challenged by judicial review in the Environment Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Register Maintenance and Annual Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (annual return); Inland Revenue Department (financial statements and RBP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual return (Form NZCN071) on the anniversary of incorporation and pay the NZ$40 annual return filing fee. Maintain the statutory registers of shareholders, directors, charges and share transfers at the registered office. Determine eligibility for financial reporting exemptions under s 206 of the Companies Act 1993; if not exempt, prepare and file financial statements in accordance with NZ IFRS or the Financial Reporting Act 2013. For a non-resident company without an NZ or Australian resident director, maintain a designated New Zealand agent for service of process and update the Companies Register accordingly.
required_dossiers: Annual return (Form NZCN071)
Financial statements (if not exempt)
Director and shareholder certificates
Register of shares, charges and directors
New Zealand agent appointment deed (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late annual returns result in a late fee and possible removal from the register; apply for restoration under s 329 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 years of removal, supported by a director's declaration that the company was carrying on business at the date of removal. Alternatively, rectify the register administratively before removal takes effect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand (Te Mana Rauhī Taiao) — Hazardous Substances Register; New Zealand Customs Service (import/transshipment declarations and Customs Controlled Area licensing); WorkSafe New Zealand (occupational safety for any NZ office or warehouse presence)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory manufacturing or industrial operating licence is mandated for pure cross-border procurement, trading and logistics arbitrage of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510). Optional instruments where goods are landed, stored or re-packaged in New Zealand: Hazardous Substance Notification / Approval (HSNO Act 1996) and Customs Controlled Area Licence (Customs and Excise Act 2018).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand (EPA New Zealand, Te Mana Rauhī Taiao)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt — No Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) required for a trading-only company with no physical manufacturing, mining or land disturbance in New Zealand. Where the company establishes a New Zealand warehouse for bonded storage of lithium carbonate, the activity is classified as 'Hazardous Substance Notification' (low-to-medium risk) subject to approval under ss 96-97 of the HSNO Act 1996, not a full EIA report; lithium carbonate (CAS 554-13-2) is generally non-classified under the GHS unless formulated with toxic impurities, in which case a Class 6.1 toxic substance approval applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process discharge in New Zealand for the procurement/arbitrage model. Conditional compliance thresholds if warehousing is established: (i) airborne particulate matter (PM10) shall not exceed the NES-AQ 24-hour average of 50 µg/m³ and annual mean of 20 µg/m³; (ii) any spill-containment wastewater must be neutralised to pH 6.0-9.0 and may be discharged only under a Regional Council water permit; (iii) storage must comply with HSNO location test standards, including segregation from foodstuffs, acids and oxidising agents, and spill clean-up residues must be managed under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No structural, civil-defence or occupational clearance is required for the non-resident shell company. If a liaison office or warehouse is opened in New Zealand: (i) Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) operational fire safety certification and an evacuation scheme under s 55 of the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; (ii) Building Warrant of Fitness and compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004 for any occupied premises exceeding 100m²; (iii) WorkSafe New Zealand workplace notification and a written Health and Safety at Work policy, including first-aid provisions, hazard register and accident reporting under the Accident Compensation Act 2001; (iv) where racked storage exceeds 5m in height, a structural load inspection certificate from a Chartered Professional Engineer is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; secure digital portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz; customs interface via New Zealand Customs Service
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated International Company applies for an Inland Revenue (IRD) number using form IR742 (Non-Resident Company Registration), supported by the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and ultimate beneficial owner disclosures required under New Zealand AML/CFT rules, and a registered New Zealand address for service or an appointed New Zealand tax agent. Submission is made through the myIR portal or by an authorised tax agent; the IRD number is ordinarily issued within 2-10 business days. GST registration for non-resident companies is processed separately under the special non-resident GST registration regime, optionally through a New Zealand agent or branch, with GST returns filed on the standard return cycle.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. The available statutory election and classification mechanisms include: (i) voluntary GST registration before the compulsory NZD 60,000 turnover threshold; (ii) GST group election under s 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (iii) GST branch election under s 56 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (iv) functional currency election under s 7A of the Income Tax Act 2007; and (v) hybrid mismatch entity/arrangement treatment under Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 implementing the OECD BEPS hybrid mismatch rules. An International Company structured as a non-resident company is outside the New Zealand income tax net for foreign-source income, provided central management and control is not exercised in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted below this threshold; non-resident suppliers carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand are subject to the same compulsory registration threshold, with special rules for offshore remote-services suppliers
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, compulsory government clearance API, or digital stamping mandate exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the PEPPOL network via accredited service providers. GST-registered suppliers must issue compliant tax invoices under s 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, showing the supplier's GST number, invoice date, description and quantity of supplies, consideration, and GST amount; simplified tax invoices are permitted for supplies under NZD 1,000, and buyer-created tax invoices are allowed in limited circumstances. Returns are filed electronically through myIR on a one-month, two-month, or six-month cycle, with no government pre-clearance of individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported goods is available under s 11(1)(c) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within the statutory timeframes (generally within 28 days of delivery to the purchaser, or within 28 days after payment if the supplier does not make delivery) and retains prescribed evidence of export. Battery-grade lithium carbonate powder physically shipped to non-resident buyers qualifies if the export entry, shipping documents, and payment records align. Services to non-residents may qualify under s 11A (remote services) when the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are not performed in New Zealand. The exporter must hold sufficient documentation to demonstrate the goods were actually exported, including transport documentation showing movement to an overseas destination and non-return to New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated New Zealand Customs export entry (Customs Export Declaration lodged via the Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and sales contract describing battery-grade lithium carbonate powder and purchaser
Packing list, weight certificate, and grade/lot analysis certificate for the lithium carbonate
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence confirming receipt of foreign currency proceeds
GST zero-rating evidence log maintained per s 24B of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including proof of export timing and destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating claims within the standard four-year reassessment period, with no time limit where fraud or evasion is involved; exporters must retain substantiating records for seven years. Incorrect zero-rating gives rise to retrospective reassessment at the 15% GST rate, recovery of any refunded output GST, use-of-money interest from the original refund date, and shortfall penalties under s 141 of the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Knowingly creating false export documentation or fraudulent zero-rating claims can additionally trigger criminal prosecution under s 143A and s 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with imprisonment of up to five years, fines, and debarment from future zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), the sole monetary authority and currency issuer for New Zealand and the Cook Islands, where New Zealand dollars are legal tender. No separate foreign-exchange administration exists; exchange-control regulations were abolished with the 1984/85 float and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 (consolidated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021), so no ministerial or central-bank approval is required for foreign-currency transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalized, free-floating currency regime with no exchange controls on either the current or capital account. Non-resident companies and offshore vehicles enjoy unrestricted conversion of NZD into foreign currency and vice versa; there are no surrender, repatriation, licensing, or prior-approval requirements for trade-related payments, capital injections, loan servicing, or profit remittance. The only gateway legislation is the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which screens non-resident acquisitions of 'sensitive' New Zealand land and significant business assets; it does not capture a treasury/procurement vehicle purchasing battery-grade lithium carbonate (ISIC 4662 / HS 2836.91) and does not impede ordinary trade settlement. Profit remittance and dividend flows are unrestricted from an FX standpoint; the only practical obstacles are fiscal, namely New Zealand non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on NZ-source dividends/interest and the approved issuer levy (AIL) alternative. For a Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) classified as non-resident of New Zealand and not carrying on business through a permanent establishment in NZ, trading income from offshore lithium purchases and resales is not NZ-source income under section YD 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to open a domiciliary foreign-currency account. Export proceeds and receivables in USD, EUR, CNY, AUD or any other currency may be retained offshore, netted against import payables, or converted at commercial banks at free-market rates. Residual compliance obligations are limited to: (i) bank reporting of balance-of-payments statistics to the Reserve Bank for transactions above NZD 50,000; (ii) AML/CTF record-keeping under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; and (iii) transfer-pricing documentation for related-party commodity flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency NZD/USD/EUR/CNY) and Capital Escrow Account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Confirmation Statement) for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: due within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate filing penalty if the annual renewal fee is paid on time; late or omitted confirmation may trigger a statutory late fee of 10% of the annual fee, and continued default for more than six months may result in administrative strike-off after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal Fee / Government Franchise Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation; registered agent will request instructions and funds no later than 14 days before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment accrues late-payment penalties under the International Companies Act fee scale; after six consecutive months of non-payment, the company may be struck off and thereafter loses legal capacity until reinstated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a standard non-licensed International Company. Independent audit is compulsory only if the company is separately licensed under Cook Islands financial-services legislation (e.g., banking, insurance, or investment business), in which case the sector regulator may impose an annual audit requirement regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting-framework designation for International Companies. If financial statements are prepared voluntarily, NZ IFRS is the accepted common framework in Cook Islands practice; local GAAP is also permissible for internal reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company is not subject to a public UBO register, but the registered agent must conduct annual customer due diligence and confirm the identity of every shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner before filing the annual confirmation. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership during the year must be entered in the Register of Members and supported by an updated ownership declaration to the registered agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of member and director resolutions
Beneficial ownership and customer due diligence records maintained by the registered agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–USD 1,200 per annum typical agent and registered-office fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if not statutorily required; if parent-group or lender requires an IFRS audit, typical cost USD 10,000–USD 18,000 for a special-purpose procurement holding entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No offshore tax-exempt zone exists in New Zealand. The 28% headline rate is reduced only by ordinary deductions, R&D tax credits (20% for eligible R&D expenditure), and the R&D loss tax credit cash-out. A non-resident IC with no fixed establishment in New Zealand and no New Zealand-sourced income is effectively outside the NZ corporate income tax net (0% NZ tax on offshore trading income), but the legal classification as 'Tax Exempt Zone' (Cook Islands International Company) confers no exemption from NZ tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Tax Return) filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal; paper filing is accepted for non-resident companies without a tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (12-month income year; standard balance date 31 March). Provisional tax payments are made in three annual installments (28 June, 28 January, 28 May) or six-monthly by ratio method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed and any residual income tax paid by 7 July. With an extension of time under a tax agent, filing may be deferred to the relevant extended due date (ordinarily the following 31 March).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the company as registered with the New Zealand Companies Office (or IRD entity name for an overseas IC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact IC name and jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., '[NAME] Ltd, Cook Islands') if a foreign company is registered as an overseas company.
Non-resident ICs must apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number before filing; non-resident companies without NZ-sourced income generally do not need an IRD number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance date relevant to the assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign balance dates are accepted for non-resident ICs; the annual return is aligned to the foreign accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income derived in or from New Zealand (gross amount before deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC with pure offshore procurement arbitrage (buying lithium carbonate in one foreign market and selling in another) should return nil NZ assessable income; any amount derived through a New Zealand fixed establishment must be returned in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure (excluding capital and non-deductible items) incurred in deriving assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenditure of a non-resident IC may be deducted only to the extent it is incurred in deriving New Zealand assessable income; head office and offshore procurement costs are non-deductible if allocated to non-NZ income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss (Box 6 minus Box 7).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC without NZ nexus, this is nil; a net loss from NZ branch operations may be carried forward subject to continuity of ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deduction of carry-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward for a non-resident IC requires 49% shareholder continuity across the loss year and the deduction year.
Non-resident IC taxed only on NZ fixed establishment income at 28%; offshore procurement arbitrage profits carry 0% NZ tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (RWT withheld, foreign tax credits, imputation credits, PAYE deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may claim foreign tax credits under the relevant DTA and uni-ateral credits under s. LJ 1 for foreign income tax actually paid on the NZ-assessable portion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax (RIT) payable (Box 11 minus Box 12) or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, RIT is nil where the company is outside the provisional tax threshold (RIT > NZD 5,000 triggers provisional tax).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZD 250 for a company failing to file the IR4 by the due date; late payment penalty on unpaid RIT: 1% on the day after the due date, 4% on the 7th day, then 1% per month cumulative; use-of-money interest applies (currently 9.53% for underpayment in 2025, subject to quarterly change); repeated non-filing may result in default assessments and prosecution fines up to NZD 50,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (NRWT on non-resident dividends paid by a New Zealand company), reduced by applicable DTA to 15% (portfolio), 5% (Australia and most treaties for companies holding 10% or more of the voting power), and 0% in limited cases for fully imputed dividends to shareholders in treaty countries under the 'fully imputed dividend' concession? Actually no - fully imputed dividends are not exempt; the imputation credit attached is not refundable to non-residents, and NRWT still applies on the cash dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the recipient must be the beneficial owner of the dividend and must deliver a valid Tax Residence Certificate issued by its home jurisdiction plus an executed IR 292 withholding declaration (or equivalent) to the New Zealand payer before payment. The New Zealand payer must retain the certificate and declaration for 7 years. Where documentation is incomplete, the payer must withhold 30%, and the recipient may claim excess NRWT as a credit/refund by filing a New Zealand income tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may substitute NRWT on interest paid by an approved issuer to a non-resident lender, eliminating NRWT. Royalties: statutory NRWT 15%; DTA rates generally 10% (e.g., China), 10-15% (OECD treaties). Lithium-carbonate trading receipts are not NZ-source royalties absent a NZ patent/licence over IP; pure trading margin is not subject to NZ WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory NZD threshold for Local File/Master File; CbC reporting is mandatory where consolidated group revenue exceeds NZD 680,000,000. Inland Revenue practice requires contemporaneous TP documentation for all material cross-border related-party transactions; transactions below NZD 1,000,000 per counterparty are generally treated as low risk. Commodity trading (including battery-grade lithium carbonate) must be benchmarked against arm's-length quoted market prices at the contract date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) codifying substance requirements; instead the Commissioner applies the central management and control test (s. YD 2) to determine tax residence, and the general anti-avoidance rule (s. BG 1) with the associated reconstructive rule (s. GA 1). A Cook Islands IC that is 'managed and controlled' from New Zealand (board meetings, strategic decisions, or bank signatories located in NZ) is a NZ tax resident on worldwide income, notwithstanding its Cook Islands tax-exempt status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (s. 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately returning nil NZ income while exercising management and control in New Zealand; suppressing income from lithium carbonate arbitrage through undisclosed bank accounts; destroying records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction: imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine up to NZD 50,000 per tax type/period; civil shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax; plus use-of-money interest and compensatory interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly make or assist false returns may be prosecuted personally; on conviction they face imprisonment and fines; Inland Revenue may issue a director penalty notice for unpaid PAYE/GST, and the court may order restitution and disqualification from managing companies for up to 5 years (Companies Act 1993 s. 382).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Cook Islands International Company with no real office, employees, or decision-making substance solely to obtain the 'Tax Exempt Zone' status while the commercial reality of the battery-metals procurement is directed from New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under s. BG 1 and s. GA 1 (the arrangement is void against the Commissioner) with reassessment at 28%; shortfall penalty of 100% for an 'abusive tax position' (or 150% if later found to be evasion); CFC attribution of undistributed income to NZ shareholders under the CFC rules can apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be judged not to have acted in good faith (Companies Act 1993 s. 135/136); civil restitution for unpaid tax, travel bans may be sought by the Commissioner where assets are being dissipated, and criminal liability for dishonesty under the Crimes Act 1961 (ss. 228-229, imprisonment up to 7 years).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing the sale of battery-grade lithium carbonate to a related NZ distributor at an inflated or deflated margin outside arm's length; failing to prepare CUP benchmarking for commodity sales; failing to file TP documentation on demand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Commissioner's adjustment to an arm's-length price under Subpart GC; shortfall penalty of 20% (unacceptable tax position), 100% (abusive tax position), or 150% (evasion) applied to the TP adjustment; interest from the due date; potential CbC disclosure penalty for failure to file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve unrealistic intercompany pricing without obtaining benchmarking are exposed to civil penalties for breach of directors' duties (s. 137 Companies Act 1993); in aggravated cases, personal liability for the tax shortfall plus conviction for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Swift_LC and wire-transfer corridors for lithium-carbonate procurement without conducting customer due diligence, or with opaque beneficial ownership (Cook Islands bearer shares), or structuring transactions to fall below reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: civil penalty up to NZD 2,000,000 for a body corporate and NZD 100,000 for an individual per contravention; orders to adopt remedial programmes; asset forfeiture under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1991 for laundering proceeds of taxation offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for a failure to maintain an AML/CFT programme (s. 59-61); penalties of up to NZD 100,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for wilful blindness; travel bans and freezing orders may be issued pending prosecution.
